uncited: *   **Input**: A query position $\mathbf{p} = (x, y, z)$ in the volume's local coordinate system, and a discrete volume dataset $V$ defined on a regular grid.
*   **Volume Data ($V$)**: A 3D array of values indexed by integer coordinates $(i, j, k)$.
The grid spacing is assumed to be uniform and normalized such that sample centers are at integer coordinates.
**Coordinate Rounding**: Round the floating-point coordinates of the query position $\mathbf{p}$ to the nearest integers.
This identifies the indices of the closest voxel.
**Lookup**: Retrieve the value from the volume dataset $V$ at the rounded integer indices.
*   $x, y, z$ are the continuous coordinates of the query point.

*   $\text{round}(\cdot)$ is the standard rounding function (rounding to the nearest integer, with ties typically rounded to the nearest even integer or away from zero depending on implementation, though the source simply states "round").
*   $V(i, j, k)$ is the value stored at grid index $(i, j, k)$.
It requires only rounding operations and a single memory lookup.
No additional buffers or neighbor lookups are required.
